entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:1
segments: The acquitting of the guilty, and the condemning of the innocent, are both an abomination to the Lord.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:4
segments:
Muzzle the ox; to prevent his eating.  The usual way of threshing grain at that time, was treading it out with oxen. 
 
The withholding of needful support and comfort even from oxen, is a sin against God; much more is the withholding of them from servants and other human beings who labor for our good, and especially from those who labor for our spiritual good.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:6
segments: Succeed--his brother; to his inheritance, and to his name in the genealogical records.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:10
segments:
Hath his shoe loosed; a sign of disgrace in view of the people. 
 
Various regulations were adopted by God to make the Israelites a peculiar people, and keep them separate from other nations.  These regulations were binding on them till the introduction of the gospel dispensation, when they were abolished, and the Jews freed from all obligations to observe them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:13
segments: A great and a small; so as to get more than just weight when he bought, and give less when he sold.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:16
segments: Strict honesty in buying and selling, and a sacred regard to what is just and right in all our dealings with men, are essential to acceptance with God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:18
segments: Taking advantage of those who are in distress, and wronging such as have not power to protect themselves, is mean and wicked.  Those who do it incur the wrath of God, and may expect to be visited with his curse.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 25:19
segments: Shall blot out the remembrance; utterly destroy them.
